plastic.tip: Empty liquids and rinse before recycling. Keep caps on.

locations.berkeley: Berkeley accepts clean rigid plastics in the blue cart.
locations.san_francisco: Rigid plastics #1-7 are accepted in the blue bin; soft plastics go to landfill.

items.bottle: Empty the bottle, rinse it, and put the cap back on before recycling.
items.cup: Rinse plastic cups. Compost certified compostable cups instead of recycling them.
items.food container: Scrape out food and rinse the container. Recycle only rigid plastic.

compost.tip: Food scraps, soiled napkins, and BPI-certified compostable packaging only.

locations.berkeley: Berkeley organics include food scraps and certified compostable packaging.

items.cup: Certified compostable cups can go in the green bin. Plastic cups cannot.
items.food container: Compost food-soiled containers only when they are certified compostable.
items.carton: Empty the carton. Compost it only when the package is certified compostable.

paper.tip: Keep clean and dry. Flatten cardboard boxes.

locations.berkeley: Berkeley recycling takes clean paper and flattened cardboard.

items.cup: Paper cups with a plastic lining usually belong in landfill unless the city accepts them.
items.food container: Flatten clean paperboard. Food-soiled paper goes to compost.

glass.tip: Rinse jar clean. Metal lids should be separated.

locations.berkeley: Berkeley accepts empty glass bottles and jars in recycling.

items.bottle: Rinse the bottle. Recycle the glass and keep non-metal caps out of the bottle.
items.cup: Rinse drinking glasses only if the city accepts them. Lids are usually landfill.
items.food container: Rinse jars. Recycle clean metal lids separately from the glass.

landfill.tip: Wrappers, chip bags, and styrofoam cannot be recycled.

locations.berkeley: When Berkeley does not list the item, use the gray landfill cart.

items.bottle: Soft plastic bottles and foam bottles go to landfill.
items.cup: Plastic-lined and styrofoam cups go to landfill.
items.food container: Chip bags and greasy wrappers go to landfill.
